title: To-do list
description:
Design a class `TodoList`. Think about the interface from the caller's side first: the table is the whole contract.

| Member | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| `int add(std::string_view title)` | adds a task and returns its id. Ids start at 1 and are never reused. An empty title is refused: returns 0 and adds nothing. |
| `bool complete(int id)` | marks the task done. Returns `false` if there is no such task or it is already done. |
| `bool remove(int id)` | deletes the task. Returns `false` if there is no such task. |
| `int pending() const` | how many tasks are not done |
| `int total() const` | how many tasks exist |
| `std::vector<std::string> titles(bool onlyPending) const` | the titles in the order they were added; with `true`, only those not yet done |

How you store the tasks is up to you (a private nested struct in a vector works well). The tests only use the public interface.
hints: Keep a `std::vector` of a small struct (id, title, done) and an `m_nextId` that only ever grows, so removed ids are never reused.
Each action searches the vector for the id first and returns `false` when it is not there.
